dimensions.name: Bank size & dedicated volume
dimensions.evidence: The bank has a substantial number of items (3519 active, 3399 served), with a high enrichment percentage (93.5%).
dimensions.gap: While the volume is impressive, the distribution across subjects is uneven, with some critical areas like cardiology and neurology underrepresented.

dimensions.name: NBME blueprint / systems coverage
dimensions.evidence: The distribution of questions is heavily skewed towards basic sciences like biochemistry and microbiology, with clinical subjects like cardiology and neurology having very few items.
dimensions.gap: The lack of balance in subject coverage means that students may not be adequately prepared for the full range of topics on the USMLE.

dimensions.name: Item craft (stem/options/clinical reasoning)
dimensions.evidence: Many items suffer from weak distractors and lack depth in explanations, with several items not meeting USMLE standards.
dimensions.gap: Improvement is needed in crafting more challenging options and providing comprehensive rationales for incorrect answers.

dimensions.name: Basic-science ↔ clinical integration
dimensions.evidence: There is a noted lack of clinical integration in many items, with some misclassified as biostats and others missing clinical reasoning.
dimensions.gap: Better integration of basic science concepts with clinical scenarios is necessary to enhance learning and application.

dimensions.name: Biostats / ethics / CCS readiness
dimensions.evidence: Biostatistics and ethics are present but not robustly covered, with some misclassifications noted.
dimensions.gap: A more thorough and accurate representation of biostats and ethics is needed to ensure readiness.

dimensions.name: Rationale / teachability
dimensions.evidence: Explanations often lack depth, with many cut off or missing complete reasoning for incorrect options.
dimensions.gap: Enhancing the depth and completeness of rationales would improve the educational value of the bank.

dimensions.name: High-yield disease & pharm readiness
dimensions.evidence: High-yield topics are covered, but the lack of balance in subject distribution affects readiness.
dimensions.gap: Ensuring a more balanced coverage of high-yield topics across all subjects would improve readiness.

dimensions.name: Quality gates & consistency
dimensions.evidence: Inconsistencies in item classification and quality of distractors are noted.
dimensions.gap: Implementing stricter quality control measures would enhance consistency and reliability.

bank.examTakerVerdict: The QBank provides a substantial volume of questions, but the uneven subject distribution and lack of depth in explanations may limit its effectiveness as a comprehensive study tool. Improvements in item craft and clinical integration are needed to meet UWorld-level standards.
